method.label: Count one solution per unit interval

annotationRationale: Fractional-part bounds restrict the possible solutions and split the equation into unit intervals. Continuity and endpoint signs establish existence, while monotonicity proved by differences establishes uniqueness. Counting the consecutive integer interval indices is a supporting step.
sourceMethod: Follows the first official solution, which compares the fractional-part graph with the parabola on unit intervals. Clarifies its intersection count using continuity, algebraic monotonicity, and explicit treatment of the excluded right endpoint.

review.mathCheck: Fractional-part bounds force \(-100<x<100\). The difference formula proves each \(H_k\) strictly increasing. Endpoint signs give exactly one zero for every \(k=-100,\ldots,98\), including \(x=0\) when \(k=0\). For \(k=99\), the only endpoint zero is the excluded 100. Thus there are \(98-(-100)+1=199\) solutions, choice C.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently worded adaptation of the first MAA solution 25, pages 12–13. It preserves fractional-part reduction and half-open interval counting, replacing the graphical assertion with explicit continuity and algebraic uniqueness arguments.
review.annotationCheck: All negative-input and endpoint cases are handled. The assessed concepts match the written proof, and integer-index counting is correctly supporting knowledge. The difference argument requires no calculus.
